findings.quote: Using one true statement plus a matching fact is the **Law of Detachment**.
findings.problem: This is too broad. The Law of Detachment specifically requires a true conditional $p$ implies $q$ together with its true hypothesis $p$, which permits conclusion $q$. Any true statement plus a vaguely "matching" fact is not sufficient. OpenStax states the required conditional-and-hypothesis structure: https://openstax.org/books/contemporary-mathematics/pages/2-7-logical-arguments

Blind-solved Example 2: converse is wet ground implies rain; inverse is no rain implies dry ground; contrapositive is dry ground implies no rain.
Blind-solved Example 3: a valid answer needs wet ground without rain, such as ground made wet by a sprinkler; the lesson instead uses a mopped floor.
Blind-solved Example 4: choice C is the contrapositive and therefore the logically equivalent statement.

findings.quote: Using one true statement plus a matching fact is the **Law of Detachment**.
findings.problem: The required conditions are not stated precisely. Detachment applies when a conditional $p$ implies $q$ is true and its hypothesis $p$ is true; the phrase "one true statement plus a matching fact" does not tell students when the rule actually applies.

illustrations.description: Draw a four-box logic map showing the original $p$ to $q$, converse $q$ to $p$, inverse not-$p$ to not-$q$, and contrapositive not-$q$ to not-$p$, with arrows labeled swap and negate and links between the equivalent pairs.
illustrations.why: A compact visual map would make the four forms and their relationships easier to distinguish and remember than four similar text lines alone.

accuracy_concerns.quote: A janitor mops the floor. The ground is wet, but it is not raining.
accuracy_concerns.concern: The example does not establish its stated hypothesis because a mopped floor is not necessarily the ground, so the proposed counterexample is invalid as written.

accuracy_concerns.quote: Using one true statement plus a matching fact is the **Law of Detachment**.
accuracy_concerns.concern: This description is overbroad. The law requires a true conditional and affirmation of that conditional's hypothesis, not merely any true statement and a matching fact.
